context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:105:The proposed “courbe modulaire pour courbes elliptiques” can be tested at a split Tate cusp using $U=E_q\setminus\{O\}$ over $\mathbf Q((q))$. This adds a local degeneration calculation to the elliptic modular family in `LM_140-2_text.tex`, scan 517. Tate’s torsion sequence $0\to\mu_n\to E_q[n]\to\mathbf Z/n\to 0$ has Kummer class $q$, so the induced inertia on $H_1(U_{\bar K},\mathbf Z_\ell)=T_\ell E_q$ is nontrivial unipotent monodromy (Tate, 1995, torsion discussion, manuscript p. 19). This verifies the author’s predicted nontriviality for the stated test case and supplies the more restrictive residual-action obstruction in RN103-05.

context/MPL_149_091-136_notes.md:145:The suggestion of a criterion “sur les groupes $p$-divisibles” is appropriate to abelian-variety data, but the Jacobian’s Barsotti–Tate group alone cannot detect every node of the curve. The compact-type construction in RN100-03 also works over a suitable mixed-characteristic trait: its Jacobian is an abelian scheme although its curve is singular, reflecting the distinction $g=\sum g_\alpha+h_1$ in `ARCH_147_003-137_text.tex`, scan 12 (Deligne & Mumford, 1969). A genuinely nonabelian replacement is available for smooth proper curves of genus at least two with a regular semistable model and an integral base point over a complete characteristic-zero DVR with perfect residue field of characteristic $p$: good reduction is equivalent to crystallinity of the unipotent $p$-adic étale fundamental group (Andreatta et al., 2015, Theorems 1.6 and 1.9). This differs from testing only the Jacobian’s $p$-divisible group and should remain separate from the prime-to-$p$ outer-inertia criterion.
